QUALITY AND COORDINATION

An Inspection and Test Plan That Supports Delivery

Define what must be checked, by whom and before which next activity.

In this insight

Build the plan around acceptance requirementsMake hold points operationally clearTrack exceptions through closureUse the plan for handover preparationFor your project discussionDiscuss a project ↗

Educational overview · Project-specific design and execution require qualified review.

Build the plan around acceptance requirements

An inspection and test plan should translate the project specification and design requirements into a usable sequence of checks. The responsible technical team determines those requirements. The project manager should ensure that the plan identifies the relevant activity, required evidence and review role. A generic checklist is unlikely to capture the interfaces that matter to a particular ground-engineering package.

Make hold points operationally clear

Where an activity cannot proceed until a required review or acceptance, make that condition visible in the programme and site workflow. Define the notice process and the information reviewers need. The commercial team should understand the associated dependencies. A hold point that is known only to the quality department can become a surprise interruption to the delivery team.

Track exceptions through closure

When a check identifies a discrepancy, record the location, relevant requirement and agreed route for assessment. Keep the responsible designer or other appropriate authority involved where necessary. Do not close an item merely because a photograph has been uploaded. Closure should reflect the accepted action and required evidence under the project’s procedures.

Use the plan for handover preparation

Link completed checks to the final document index so evidence is accumulated progressively. Review missing records while the work and personnel are still available. This reduces the risk of a late administrative gap delaying acceptance. A useful inspection plan supports both construction decisions and a coherent handover, with a clear distinction between work performed and evidence reviewed.

For your project discussion

Use these questions to structure a conversation with the project’s qualified design and delivery team. This article is general procurement guidance, not a site-specific design, method statement or compliance assessment. The cited international resources provide background; applicable local requirements and the approved project documents govern the work.

Take this into your next conversation

  • Derive checks from the actual specification.
  • Link hold points to programme activities.
  • Close exceptions with the required evidence.
